bluf: Ukraine is stabilizing the frontline and making territorial gains, aided by the disruption of Russian logistics and Starlink access, while Russian forces suffer unsustainable losses. Concurrently, Iran is leveraging the ceasefire to normalize its protection racket over the Strait of Hormuz, threatening global energy transit and drawing NATO and South Korea into consideration of maritime security operations. The Kremlin’s failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal with China underscores deepening strategic constraints, while the US-Iran negotiations remain deadlocked over nuclear and strait issues.

sections.title: Ukraine Conflict Dynamics
sections.content: Ukraine's defensive operations are stabilizing the frontline, with NATO Secretary General Rutte and the US DIA confirming Ukrainian territorial gains following Russia's loss of Starlink access in February 2026. Ukrainian forces are inflicting heavy losses on Russian troops, averaging over 1,000 casualties per day in 2026, and have disrupted Russian logistics through strikes on critical infrastructure, including the Moscow Oil Refinery and the Angstrem Semiconductor Plant. Russia's large-scale drone and missile strikes on May 17-18, targeting Dnipro and Odesa with 546 munitions, failed to achieve decisive effect and damaged a Chinese-owned ship, highlighting the risk of collateral damage. The Kremlin remains committed to seizing Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, but internal elite recognition of a 'dead end' and Putin's failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal with China indicate mounting strategic pressure.
sources: Ukraine’s Fortress Belt: The Key to Sustaining the Frontline

sections.title: Iranian Strait of Hormuz and Nuclear Negotiations
sections.content: Iran is using the ceasefire to institutionalize its de facto control over the Strait of Hormuz through a protection racket, compelling vessels to pay 'security' fees to avoid attack by Iranian forces. US-Iran negotiations have made only 'slight progress,' with Iran refusing to commit to suspending uranium enrichment or handing over its HEU stockpile, and demanding formal recognition of its strait control. The US has seized two Iranian-linked oil tankers, and Trump canceled a planned military strike on May 19 after Qatari, Emirati, and Saudi leaders requested a pause. Iran is also reconstituting its drone and missile programs and has studied US aircraft flight patterns for targeting, while NATO countries consider a maritime escort mission starting in July. South Korea is reviewing participation in the US-led Maritime Freedom Construct after an Iranian attack on a South Korean-operated vessel, the Namu-ho, on May 4.

sections.title: Russia-Belarus Nuclear Posturing and Occupation Policies
sections.content: Russia and Belarus completed combined nuclear exercises on May 21, including the deployment of nuclear munitions to Belarus and launches of ICBMs and hypersonic missiles, highlighting Moscow's deepening de facto control over Minsk. The unannounced exercise, involving over 64,000 personnel, is aimed at posturing strength and distracting from battlefield weaknesses in Ukraine. Meanwhile, Russian occupation authorities continue systemic integration of occupied Ukrainian territories, including forced transfer of children for medical operations, military-style training for teenagers, and cultural integration programs. Russia is also formalizing lower barriers for Russian investment and real estate purchases in occupied areas, and VTB Bank is expanding its coercive bureaucratic influence.

key_developments: Ukraine stabilizes frontline and makes territorial gains; Russian forces suffer over 1,000 casualties per day.
Iran uses ceasefire to normalize protection racket over Strait of Hormuz, demanding fees for safe passage.
US-Iran talks deadlocked; Iran refuses to suspend enrichment or hand over HEU; US seizes two Iranian-linked tankers.
Russia-Belarus nuclear exercises signal deepened control over Minsk; Putin fails to secure Power of Siberia-2 deal with China.
South Korea reviews joining US-led maritime security coalition after Iranian attack on its vessel.
outlook: Ukraine's defensive gains and Russian attrition suggest the frontline will remain contested but stable, while the Kremlin's economic constraints and failed China deal may force a strategic recalibration. Iran will likely continue to exploit the ceasefire to consolidate strait control, risking a NATO-led maritime escalation and potential military confrontation if negotiations collapse.
